methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous integrated genomic and transcriptomic study of 21 relapsed multiple myeloma patients after anti-GPRC5D TCE therapy with comprehensive multi-omics analysis: whole-genome sequencing (WGS), single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), single-cell ATAC-seq (scATAC-seq), flow cytometry, western blot, and immunofluorescence. WGS using multiple variant callers (Mutect2, Strelka2, Lancet, Manta) for SNVs, indels, and structural variants. Copy-number analysis using BICSEQ2 and CNVkit. Functional validation using engineered cell lines and patient CD138+ plasma cells. Detailed methods with appropriate statistical approaches for variant calling and analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Mechanistic study of treatment resistance to anti-GPRC5D T cell engagers in multiple myeloma. Identifies three distinct GPRC5D escape mechanisms: (1) focal/biallelic deletions (68.4% of cases); (2) monoallelic deletion with variants on remaining allele; (3) epigenetic silencing. Directly relevant to understanding acquired resistance and informing development of next-generation TCEs. Demonstrates differential targeting of escape variants by TCEs with varying epitope specificity and valency, suggesting therapeutic strategies to overcome resistance.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive reporting of genomic methods with appropriate detail for reproducibility. Whole-genome sequencing data submitted to appropriate repository (GEO accession GSE199373). Extensive supplementary tables documenting patient samples, mutations, and annotations. Lentiviral constructs and GPRC5D-expressing cell lines available upon request. Methods section thoroughly describes WGS pipeline, bioinformatic analysis, and functional validation approaches. Flow cytometry gating strategies provided.

novelty_literature.justification: First comprehensive characterization of resistance mechanisms to anti-GPRC5D T cell engagers in multiple myeloma. Novel discovery of three distinct escape pathways operating in >68% of relapsed cases. Demonstrates multimodal antigenic escape including functional effects of variants on protein trafficking (ER trapping) vs epitope mutation. Shows TCE-epitope specific selection pressures creating convergent evolutionary trajectories. Identifies therapeutic opportunities through valency and epitope-matched TCE combinations.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript presenting complex multi-omic data clearly. Abstract concisely summarizes three escape mechanisms and therapeutic implications. Methods section comprehensive with appropriate technical detail. Results logically presented from genomic findings through mechanistic validation in cell lines. Figures effectively display genomic alterations (oncoplots), single-cell data (scRNA-seq clusters), and functional validation (flow cytometry, western blot). Discussion contextualizes findings within tumor evolution and resistance biology.

key_strengths: Comprehensive multi-omic characterization of resistance mechanisms to anti-GPRC5D TCE therapy in multiple myeloma with detailed genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic analyses
Discovery of three distinct antigenic escape pathways (biallelic deletions 68.4%, monoallelic deletion with variants, epigenetic silencing) operating in relapsed patients
Functional validation demonstrating that GPRC5D variants cause ER retention and impaired trafficking rather than simple epitope loss, distinguishing mechanisms
Evidence that different TCEs with varying epitope specificity, affinity, and valency select for different GPRC5D escape variants, suggesting rational combination strategies
Multiple convergent subclones within individual patients bearing distinct GPRC5D alterations, indicating strong selection pressure and evolutionary dynamics
key_concerns: Observational case series (n=21) without randomization or control groups; cannot establish causality of TCE selection pressure vs patient-intrinsic factors
Limited clinical outcome data; study focuses on genomic/mechanistic characterization without linking specific resistance mechanisms to progression-free survival or response duration
Functional validation limited to engineered cell lines and ex vivo patient samples; in vivo modeling of resistance would strengthen mechanistic claims
Some analyses rely on mathematical tools with unvalidated parameters (e.g., ER trapping prediction); independent confirmation using alternative methods would strengthen conclusions
No prospective validation: future studies in large prospective cohorts with standardized sampling protocols would improve generalizability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous mechanistic study providing important insights into resistance to novel immunotherapy. Discovery of three GPRC5D escape pathways and their functional consequences informs TCE development strategies. Appropriate for Tier 2 journals with solid methodology and clinically relevant findings in high-need disease, though limited by observational design and lack of clinical outcome linkages.
